subject: astronomy
title: Moon Phases: Foundations
welcome_lead: The Moon doesn't change shape — only how much of its lit side we see.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: phases of the Moon, lunar cycle.
final_note: Eight phases, one cycle — and roughly 29 days from new to new.

concepts.def: Shape of the lit Moon we see.
Moon is between Earth and Sun — looks dark.
Earth between Sun and Moon — fully lit face.
Less than half the Moon is lit.
More than half but not full.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Moon orbits Earth. The Sun lights up one half. As the Moon moves, we see different amounts of the lit side. That's a phase.
New, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent — then back to new.
One full cycle takes about 29.5 days. That's why ancient calendars used the Moon — months come from it.
